Fixes bug B-main-red-sqlite3-approvals-harness: On base a68e4b36f, tests/test_arch_deps.py::test_ratchet_violations_match_baseline fails: sqlite3 has NEW importer outside its declared home, ddflow.services.approvals.harness. Reproduced on an exported copy of the base with no lane change.

sqlite3 has no declared home, so a new module would be a new importer too: the read-only query moves to infra.store._schema, which already imports it. harness.py loses the import and the baseline stays as it is.

Fixes bug B-main-red-sqlite3-approvals-harness: On base a68e4b36f, tests/test_arch_deps.py::test_ratchet_violations_match_baseline fails: sqlite3 has NEW importer outside its declared home, ddflow.services.approvals.harness. Reproduced on an exported copy of the base with no lane change.

sqlite3 has no declared home, so a new module would be a new importer too: the read-only query moves to infra.store._schema, which already imports it. harness.py loses the import and the baseline stays as it is.

infra.store._schema and store/__init__ are held by B-quota-meters, so the helper lands in infra.docindex instead: it already imports sqlite3 and is the module that opens SQLite read-only.

evidence.note: archdeps: sqlite3 has no declared home, so every current importer is the baseline and a new module would be one more; the http family counts urllib.parse too, hence as_uri not quote (trailers.py already does this). infra.store files are held by B-quota-meters; infra.docindex already imports sqlite3 and reads it read-only.
r-adapters and the ratchet docstring: move the import behind infra, lower the baseline in the same change (http row dropped), no new baseline entry; guard not loosened.

chunk_findings.detail: The docstring promises that "A file that cannot be read for any reason ... is no rows," but the implementation calls `path.resolve().as_uri()` before entering the `try/except sqlite3.Error`. `Path.resolve()` can raise `OSError` for reasons other than a missing file—e.g., `OSError: [Errno 40] Too many levels of symbolic links` on a cyclic symlink, or `PermissionError` when a parent directory lacks search permission. Those exceptions are not caught, so the function crashes instead of returning `[]`. This is a regression from the previous harness code, which passed the path straight to `sqlite3.connect` and therefore only saw `sqlite3.Error` failures. To reproduce: create a self-referential symlink `ln -s loop loop` and call `read_only_rows(Path("loop"), "SELECT 1")`; it raises `OSError` rather than returning `[]`.

chunk_findings.detail: A symlink-loop path such as `/tmp/a` -> `/tmp/b` and `/tmp/b` -> `/tmp/a` causes `path.resolve()` to raise `RuntimeError`, but the helper only catches `(sqlite3.Error, OSError)`. The docstring promises that an unreadable file returns no rows, and the old `harness.py` code passed a quoted `str(path)` to SQLite, whose ELOOP became a caught `sqlite3.OperationalError`. With this change, `read_only_rows` raises instead of returning `[]`, so a symlink-loop path can crash callers.
